## Owned tasks and atomic audit

| Surface | Cost and scaling |
|---|---|
| Drain | **One extra Tokio task per bound AfterAssign call**, not an executable or timer. Service handles and project/role/instance/seat metadata are cloned. The unchanged unpaged queued-request read retains complete bodies; work still scales with queued requests and bytes. Each request keeps #135's role admission gate from claim through settlement/requeue. |
| Drain cancellation | After spawn admission, dropping the waiter no longer drops the drain. Concurrent assignments can retain several tasks/queue snapshots waiting on the same role gate; no new concurrency or whole-operation deadline cap. Existing delivery/model work can continue after cancellation intentionally. |
| Close notice | **One Tokio task per nonquiet delivered close, or authorized manual re-close of an owed row**. It performs one held FYI attempt and, on admission, one schema-checked owned transaction updating notice owed to told. Quiet/requester-self closes skip it. A failed attempt remains owed for a later command; no background retry loop or sweep. |
| Notice retention | The task clones a full ClosedRoleRequest, including its original body although the FYI uses metadata. Stable IDs dedupe notices, not concurrent retry tasks/SQL attempts. Retention follows simultaneous attempts and payload bytes. A committed owed row can still need manual replay when cancellation precedes notice-task admission. |
| Atomic close audit | Each successful user withdraw/new delivered close appends **one request.closed_by_actor row in the same transaction** as INSERT-SELECT to closed history and DELETE from open requests. No append on a no-move result. Actor/caller metadata is serialized, not the request body. Append failure rolls back the state change instead of reducing audit cost by silently closing unaudited. |
| Publication | The handler enters publish_committed_batch before the mutation: one owned publication task, with the store's owned write inside it. Global publication ordering now spans schema/transaction work **and the post-commit closed/open-row read**, then broadcast. It replaces the old separate post-close audit transaction; it does not add a second audit transaction. |
| No-op/replay | Wrong-state/racing close attempts can still pay publication-lock wait, a no-row transaction and outcome reads. An already-closed owed notice retry does not repeat the close/audit; told/quiet replay adds no notice. The drain's internal self-request close has no externally asserted-actor audit. |

The new task and append costs are command/assignment driven, not per seat per watchdog tick. No new executable launch site, timer, poll or query loop. The existing held-delivery/queue/SQL work is not zero merely because it is reused.

## Other delta and C32

Recorded-prime authority removes the former designation/role-inventory reads from the privileged path; project-assignment history and project-list reads remain where needed. Caller resolution still uses the existing pane/identity/liveness machinery. Unique-instance refusal advice adds **O(H^2)** comparisons for H holders, with no extra SQL/launch. Failed holdings reads now preserve the window name and avoid a rename.

Under clarified C32(3), the actor-asserting action itself is audited atomically. Source now follows that form rather than a logged best-effort append after commitment. The previous audit-failure concern is superseded by 31b1173. Herring owns the full signal-only/binding/narrow-authority/exact-Known-limit grade; this cost pass does not replace that verdict or reopen accepted F88/PRD 003 req-10.

The final hostile-holder change is test-only: real `/bin/sh` splits both state-look and release guidance exactly and writes no payload files. Printed repair commands remain guidance, not new runtime launches.
